title: How To Rid Your Classroom Of Student Interruptions uptions/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin explains how student interruptions can derail a teacher's best lessons and offers a simple three-step method to eliminate them. First, when interrupted, the teacher should not respond verbally but instead make calm, steady eye contact. Second, the teacher pauses for five to ten seconds, letting the weight of the interruption sink in for the whole class without singling anyone out verbally. Third, the teacher calmly enforces the classroom management plan's consequence and moves on as if nothing happened. He explains that answering an interruption directly only grants permission for more interruptions to follow. The payoff, he argues, is a newfound freedom for the teacher to be passionate, humorous, or dramatic without fear of a lesson being derailed.
points: Responding to an interruption verbally, even briefly, grants implicit permission for future interruptions.
The first response to an interruption should be silent, steady eye contact rather than words.
A five-to-ten second pause lets the weight of the interruption sink in for the whole class without a verbal lecture.
The final step is calmly enforcing the classroom management plan's consequence, then moving on as if nothing happened.
Eliminating interruptions frees a teacher to be passionate, dramatic, or humorous without fear of losing the moment.
quotes: The truth is, interruptions of any kind, special moments or not, can profoundly affect your ability to motivate and inspire your students.

When a student interrupts, it’s easy to fall into the trap of answering or responding to the interruption. But doing so will grant permission to anyone and everyone to barge in and ask, comment, or opine whenever the mood strikes.
While continuing eye contact, pause for five to ten seconds to allow the weight of the interruption, and the supreme downer it causes, to sink in.
All unwanted behavior, no matter how innocent, must be backed by your classroom management plan.

This simple, ten-second strategy will forever eliminate interruptions from your classroom, and in a way that doesn’t feel harsh, involve a cutting rebuke, or discourage polite, appropriate means of participation.
